newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Guiana freedom leader accuses France of frame-up.
newsitem.headline: Guiana freedom leader accuses France of frame-up.

text.p: A leading member of French Guiana's freedom movement arrested last month on arson charges has accused France of a frame-up in an effort to destroy the independence movement in its South American territory.

Fabien Canavy told state-owned television on Wednesday: "I believe this is an organised frame-up (by France) to cut off the head of progressive movements (in Guiana) ... They use 22 and 23 year old youths, already psychologically fragile and destabilise them to extort false testimony.
"France must understand that it is time that this frame-up stops, that this masked ball is halted."

Canavy, leader of the Guiana Workers Union (UTG), and nine others were arrested in April and charged with setting fire to the home of state prosecutor Jean-Luc Beck during riots last November in French Guiana's capital Cayenne.

They were transfered to the French Caribbean island of Martinique -- their transfer necessitated since French law prohibits a magistrate personally involved in an incident to proceed with prosecution.
Jean Charpenel, the prosecutor handling the case described the attack as "attempted murder."
Canavy was released on Tuesday but remains charged. The nine others remain in jail.
Canavy along with Alain Michel, Jean-Victor Castor and Jean-Claude Ringuet are leading members of unions and political parties that favour French Guiana's independence from France.

Four others are aged 23 and younger and Canavy said interrogators pressured the younger members into making statements incriminating him, Michel, Castor and Ringuet -- statements that Canavy said they have since retracted.
Their arrest has triggered a new wave of riots in the last two weeks.
Para-military riot police flown in from mainland France clashed with hooded and armed demonstrators in the Cayenne's centre for three nights. Eleven police were injured.
The riots have shattered French Guiana's tranquil facade and laid bare economic, political and social woes.
French Guiana's economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
